description: Search the Recall Canary index of U.S. federal product recalls (FDA, FSIS, CPSC, NHTSA) by keyword, agency, severity, category, distribution state, hazard, firm, lifecycle (open or ended), or date window. Results also hold FSIS public health alerts and CPSC safety warnings, which are not recalls (`record_kind`). Returns up to 50 matching records per page (fewer with `limit`) with abbreviated content (title, firm, severity, date, the Recall Canary page URL to link when citing it, and the agency notice URL); call get_recall to fetch the full record. With a keyword, the best matches come first, open records before ended ones on each page, unless `sort` says otherwise. Unknown agency, severity, category, state, status and date values are rejected with an error message describing the allowed values. An unknown `hazard` or `firm` is also an error. Read-only.

agency.description: Issuing agencies; matches any. Case-insensitive; values are uppercase.

category.description: Single-select product category. Case-insensitive; values are uppercase.

date.description: Relative window, resolved against the request clock. Ignored when `from` or `to` is set.

firm.description: Firm slug: `firm.slug` of a record, or the last part of a /firm/ URL ("acme-foods"). Unknown is an error.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound, YYYY-MM-DD at 00:00:00 UTC.

hazard.description: Single-select hazard tag, lowercase and hyphenated, the same filter as the website hazard pages: matches records whose hazard_tags include it, press releases included. Anything else is an error.

limit.description: Return only the first `limit` rows of the page (default 50). Use a small limit, such as 5, when you only need the best few matches. `page` still counts in 50s: a cut is marked (`mcp_truncated.results`, `has_more` true) and its other rows are reached by calling again without `limit`, never by `page` + 1. By relevance, open records come first, so a small limit can cut an ended match.

page.description: 1-based, 50 records a page, at most 200 (larger is refused; narrow the date window instead).

q.description: Free-text query; omit `q` to browse by filters. Every word must match, in any order (words of 3+ letters also as prefixes, plurals as singulars); a double-quoted run is an exact phrase; an uppercase OR between two words matches either. Codes (UPC, NDC, lot, recall and campaign numbers) match as printed or as bare digits. If no record matches every word, results match only SOME and say `relaxed: true`. By relevance, each 50-row page lists open records before ended ones (exact up to 50 matches). Zero results is never a clearance: also search the brand or product name.

severity.description: Matches any. The issuing agency's own level on one scale; CPSC records and preliminary press releases are UNKNOWN.

sort.description: `relevance` (the default with `q`): best matches first, open before ended on each page. `recent`: newest first (the default without `q`). `severity`: CRITICAL, then MODERATE, newest first within each.

state.description: Two-letter USPS code ("TX") for a state or DC; matches records distributed there or nationwide.

status.description: Lifecycle, the same filter as `/data/recalls?status=` (api 2.8.0): `open` excludes ended recalls, FSIS public health alerts and CPSC safety warnings, and keeps preliminary press releases; `ended` lists ended recalls only. Case-insensitive; values are lowercase. Anything else is an error.

to.description: Inclusive upper bound, YYYY-MM-DD at 23:59:59 UTC.

name: search_recalls

outputSchema.description: A page of search or browse results. `relaxed` true means the results match only SOME of the query words, and `notices` says so.

filters.description: The filters as applied, after normalization. An unapplied filter is echoed as null or [].

html_url.description: Absolute URL of the human-readable page.

mcp_truncated.description: Present only when `limit` cut this page: the first `shown` of its `page_rows` rows (never a total).

notes.description: The caveat that absence of a match is not a clearance.

notices.description: Rules that narrowed or widened the results, and what a zero-result code search means. Often empty.

has_more.description: True when more rows exist: a next page, or rows `limit` cut (then `mcp_truncated.results` is present).

next.description: The next page as a `/data/recalls` HTTP URL. With this tool, pass `page` + 1 while `has_more` is true and `mcp_truncated.results` is absent. Null when the only further rows are this page's `limit`-cut rows.

items.description: One compacted listing row; null-valued keys are omitted. Every row carries `display_title` or `title`.

agency.description: Known values: FDA, FDA_IRES, FSIS, CPSC, NHTSA, ADMIN.

ai_generated.description: Provenance for the fields this row carries. Absent when the row carries none.

category.description: True only for a press release's model-classified category.
Known values: FOOD, DRUG, BIOLOGIC, DEVICE, COSMETIC, CONSUMER_PRODUCT, VEHICLE, AUTO_EQUIPMENT.

late.description: Present only when the recall is late.

retroactive.description: The agency's own text says the recall was reported retroactively.

record_type.description: `preliminary`: an agency press release with no canonical record yet.

risk.description: The agency rating as the page shows it (for example "High risk" for an FDA Class I recall). Null where the page shows no risk line.

explained_at.description: Absolute URL of the page that explains the rating.

warnings.description: NHTSA only, present when the campaign carries both warnings: ["Do not drive", "Park outside"].

source_recall_id.description: Agency key; a CPSC one can be stale.

source_url.description: The agency's own notice: the source of record. Name it beside `url` when you cite the record.

title.description: Only without `display_title`: the title the site shows. Not model-written.

url.description: The Recall Canary page for this record (absolute, canonical): the plain-language page a reader can use. Link this when you cite the record.

snapshot_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC response-generation time, second precision. First key on purpose.

title: Search U.S. federal product recalls
